issues.legal_issue: A subordinate court’s erroneous interpretation of the governing rent law does not justify revisional or special-leave interference when the error concerns the merits and the court had jurisdiction to decide the matter.
material_facts: The matter came to the Supreme Court by special leave after the High Court summarily dismissed an application under Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking revision of a decision made in a rent-control appeal.
The appellate court had jurisdiction to decide the dispute over possession and arrears under the rent-control law.
The appellate court construed the rent provisions incorrectly and granted possession when, on the correct construction, that relief was not available.
The alleged error concerned the appellate court’s decision on the merits, not an assumption of jurisdiction it lacked or a refusal to exercise jurisdiction it possessed.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not interfere in revision merely because the appellate court had misconstrued the rent provisions, and the Supreme Court likewise declined to interfere under Article 136; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure permits revision where a subordinate court exercises jurisdiction not vested in it, fails to exercise jurisdiction vested in it, or acts illegally or with material irregularity in exercising jurisdiction; an error of law or fact in deciding a matter within the court’s jurisdiction is not, by itself, sufficient. Article 136 does not warrant interference where the revisional court was not entitled to interfere. The Court relied on Abbasbhai v. Gulamnabi, Balakrishna Udayar v. Vasudeva Aiyar, Joy Chand Lal v. Kamalaksha Chaudhury, Manindra Land and Building Corporation Ltd. v. Bhutnath Banerjee, and Pandurang Dhondi Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav, applying the distinction between errors affecting jurisdiction and errors made while exercising jurisdiction. The relevant rent-law context included Sections 12, 28 and 29 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_revision_dismi: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal following dismissal of an application to revise a subordinate court’s decision.
predicates.subordinate_court_had_decisional_jurisdi: The subordinate court had jurisdiction to decide the kind of dispute before it.
predicates.court_decided_question_within_its_jurisd: The subordinate court decided the disputed question as part of exercising its jurisdiction.
predicates.error_was_only_on_the_merits: The asserted error concerned the correctness of the decision and did not involve exercising jurisdiction not possessed or refusing to exercise jurisdiction possessed.

issues.definition: When a special-leave appeal follows dismissal of a revision application, and the subordinate court had and exercised jurisdiction to decide the dispute, a merits-only error does not produce the stated unavailability of revisional and special-leave interference.
